All indicators gathered and cross-verified against the exported payload files. Here is the incident report.

---

## Incident Report — Traffic Analysis, 2022-01-07

### 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **192.168.1.216** |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (confirmed via DHCP option 12, NBNS name registration, and NTLMSSP hostname field) |
| Windows domain/workgroup | **SPOONWATCH** (Active Directory domain `spoonwatch.net`, DC `SPOONWATCH-DC`) |
| Logged-in user account | **steve.smith** (confirmed via SMB2/NTLMSSP authentication: domain `SPOONWATCH`, user `steve.smith`, and Kerberos `CNameString steve.smith`) |

The host's legitimate background traffic (Windows Update, Delivery Optimization, MSN/Bing, telemetry to `*.events.data.microsoft.com`) is present and consistent with normal enterprise Windows 10/11 operation, and is unrelated to the compromise.

### 2. Malware Family

**Vidar Stealer** — attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed**. No Suricata/IDS alert export was present in the evidence set, and no file in this capture was matched against an external hash/signature database (per instructions, no internet lookups were performed). The classification is based on a highly distinctive, well-documented TTP observed directly in the capture:

1. The infected host makes seven sequential HTTP POST "beacon" requests to a single C2 IP, each requesting a numbered file with a `.jpg` extension (`6.jpg, 1.jpg, 2.jpg, 3.jpg, 4.jpg, 5.jpg, 7.jpg`).
2. The C2 responds `200 OK` with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` for every request, but the response bodies all begin with an `MZ`/`PE` header — i.e., genuine Windows PE binaries mislabeled as images.
3. The response sizes closely match the known Vidar/Arkei-family module set used to read browser-stored credentials via the Mozilla NSS API (`mozglue.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `sqlite3.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll` — approximate size classes: ~83KB, ~144KB, ~137KB, ~334KB, ~440KB, ~645KB, ~1.24MB, all observed here).
4. Immediately after staging these modules, the host performs a gate check-in (`POST /osk//main.php`) followed by a final `POST /osk/` that uploads a **PKZIP archive** (`_5861695120.zip`, 379,629 bytes) as the request body — the classic Vidar "collected data" exfiltration step (credentials/cookies/autofill/screenshots bundled and POSTed back to the panel).

This staged-DLL-then-exfil-zip sequence over plaintext HTTP POST to a bare-IP C2 is the signature workflow of Vidar (and closely related Arkei-lineage stealers); no other malware family in common use reproduces this exact download/upload chain. The capture begins after initial execution — no delivery vector (phishing email, dropper download, macro) is present in the traffic, so the infection vector itself cannot be established from this evidence alone.

### 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP, plaintext HTTP, no TLS, no DNS lookup preceding it — hardcoded IP)
- Server banner: `Apache/2.4.12 (Win32) OpenSSL/1.0.1m PHP/5.3.29 mod_wsgi/4.4.11 Python/2.7.10`
- Client TCP source port: 49738; session ran 2022-01-07 20:07:32–20:07:36 (capture-relative timestamps, UTC+4)

**Malicious domains**
- None observed. C2 communication used a raw IP address with no accompanying DNS resolution.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` (bot gate check-in)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (final POST — data exfiltration)

Requests used a fixed multipart User-Agent-less header set with `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` and `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16` — a fingerprint consistent with a hardcoded HTTP library rather than a real browser.

**Transferred files (downloaded PE payloads, disguised as JPEGs)**

| Retrieved as | Size (bytes) | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 6.jpg | 144,848 | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff299508` |
| 1.jpg | 645,592 | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab1766` |
| 2.jpg | 334,288 | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090b` |
| 3.jpg | 137,168 | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9c` |
| 4.jpg | 440,120 | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d` |
| 5.jpg | 1,246,160 | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d7` |
| 7.jpg | 83,784 | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14` |

**Transferred file (uploaded/exfiltrated)**

| File | Size (bytes) | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `_5861695120.zip` (POSTed to `/osk/`, disguised as a plain form-data upload; PKZIP magic `PK\x03\x04` confirmed) | 379,629 | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07` |

### 4. Non-malicious traffic noted (ruled out)

- `download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.x, 8.253.189.126) — legitimate Windows Update/Delivery Optimization `.cab` and `am_delta_patch` Defender signature downloads; verified as standard Microsoft update file names/paths.
- `api.msn.com`, `www.bing.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `*.prod.do.dsp.mp.microsoft.com` — standard Windows/Edge telemetry and background services.
- Local broadcast/mDNS/SSDP/LLMNR/NBNS/Kerberos/LDAP traffic to `192.168.1.2` and `spoonwatch.net` — normal AD domain member chatter, used only to confirm hostname/user identity above.

### Summary

`192.168.1.216` (DESKTOP-GXMYNO2, domain SPOONWATCH, user **steve.smith**) is infected with an infostealer whose traffic pattern is behaviorally consistent with **Vidar Stealer**. It staged seven browser-decryption DLLs disguised as JPEGs from `2.56.57.108:80/osk/`, checked in via `main.php`, and exfiltrated a 379,629-byte ZIP of harvested data back to the same host. No signature/AV confirmation exists in the provided evidence; recommend isolating the host, resetting `steve.smith`'s credentials (domain and any stored browser/app passwords), and blocking `2.56.57.108` at the perimeter.
